title: Aerial autonomy, beyond ideal conditions.
description: Aerial robotics and multi-drone systems research at ISR-Lisboa, Instituto Superior Técnico. Explore our experimental work in perception, planning, robot design and cooperation.

hero.summary: We develop aerial robots and multi-drone systems for missions where information, energy and connectivity are limited.

introduction.heading: From the robot to the team.
introduction.text: Our research connects custom aerial platforms with onboard perception, planning and cooperation. We develop the methods and build the robots, bringing algorithms into real experimental settings.

featured.heading: Choosing what to explore next.
featured.summary: How can a team map an unknown environment without duplicating its work? Probabilistic frontier prioritization keeps exploration choices flexible as the map evolves.

themes.title: Localization & cooperative perception
themes.summary: Estimating motion and relative position when observations are uncertain or intermittent.
themes.example: Reliability-aware LiDAR-inertial odometry weights observations using physical signal and geometric quality cues. Semi-cooperative relative localization shares motion information between UAVs.

themes.title: Multimodal aerial robots
themes.summary: Combining flight with surface motion and adapting the platform to the task.
themes.example: From a rolling–flying robot and BogieCopter to a trimodal vehicle, we study how shared actuators can support different forms of locomotion.

themes.title: Aerial deployment & recovery
themes.summary: Transporting smaller UAVs closer to a mission and recovering stable flight after release.
themes.example: Complementary studies investigate release dynamics, recovery control and onboard stabilization. The tailsitter two-stage recovery study is evaluated in simulation.

themes.title: Exploration & mapping
themes.summary: Building a map while deciding where each UAV should observe next.
themes.example: Frontier reasoning, soft clustering and kinodynamically feasible trajectories help robots distribute exploration and reach informative viewpoints.

themes.title: Communication-aware coordination
themes.summary: Planning cooperation around the information that moving UAVs can exchange.
themes.example: SpArC-NARTs plans coverage under intermittent communication, accounting for sensing, energy and radio performance. The work complements a survey of communication and motion awareness.

themes.title: Target localization & tracking
themes.summary: Maintaining target awareness through sensing gaps, occlusions and changing viewpoints.
themes.example: Visual detection and multi-object tracking preserve a selected person’s identity and support following after temporary occlusion. Complementary acoustic and LiDAR work studies other sensing conditions.

themes.title: Human supervision & mixed reality
themes.summary: Placing mission information and interaction in their spatial context.
themes.example: A published mixed-reality interface supports mission interaction. Persistent human–swarm supervision and uncertainty-guided attention are broader research directions.

people.heading: Research is a team effort.
people.text: Our projects bring together doctoral researchers, students, alumni and collaborators. Meet some of the researchers whose work shapes our programme.

join.heading: Build the next experiment with us.
join.text: Interested in a research thesis or a collaboration? Tell us about your interests in aerial robotics, the problem you want to explore, and your relevant experience.
